about: Lesson E24, specification gaming. Computed by tools/school/fill_gaming.mjs from system/school/gaming.mjs, the attention lab's own model, trainer and corpus generator. Do not edit by hand. Rewards and correctness are shares of the 256 held-out prompts; every checkpoint uses the same prompts and the same sampling seed, so two checkpoints differ only by the policy.

recipe.optimiser: REINFORCE: advantage = reward - batch mean reward; loss = -(1/B) sum_b A_b sum_k log p(a_bk); Adam, no weight decay, gradient clip 1

task.about: The task: a who prompt in the corpus generator's grammar, opening with a decoy sentence (a local sentence, usually naming a guide), then the deed, then 0 or 1 distractor, cut at "?". The answer is at most 3 words, ended by "."; it is correct when it is exactly the guide who did the deed and then ".". The truth is the generator's exact next-word odds after the prompt (corpus-grammar.mjs), which put probability 1 on that guide for every prompt here. decoyShare is the share of the 256 held-out prompts whose first word is a guide who did not do the deed (a policy answering "the first name" is wrong there). Chance among three guides is 1/3.

checkers.about: Checkers, each scoring an answer (the words before ".", at most 3) against the truth guide g. gamed: the answer contains g anywhere (the loophole its author had in mind: naming every guide always contains g). patched: the first word is g and no other guide is named (closes the listing loophole). fixed: patched, and the answer must stop with "." within 3 words. exact: the answer is exactly g then ".", the truth itself. The optimiser sees only the reward.

start200.about: Start: the attention lab's model rebuilt at step 200 of its own training (same seeds as model.json), before it learned to look back; near chance on these prompts. REINFORCE against each checker for 800 steps, batch 32, learning rate 0.001, seeds 1, 2, 3 (prompt stream 10 + seed, sampling stream 20 + seed). start is the step-0 score; end is over seeds at step 800; reward is the run's own checker on the held-out prompts; peakCorrect is each seed's best checkpoint; firstStepCorrectBelow is the first checkpoint where correctness is under half its step-0 value (null if never). curveMean averages the seeds at every checkpoint.

start2000.about: Start: the trained attention model (step 2000), already right on nearly every prompt. Same recipe, gamed and patched checkers only. This asks whether a loophole is taken when the honest answer already earns full reward.

correlation.about: Pearson correlation, per seed, between reward and correctness across the checkpoints of a run. evalReward: the run's own checker on the held-out prompts (at every checkpoint including step 0) against correctness on the same sampled answers; for the exact checker the two are the same number, so its 1 is the pipeline check, not a finding. trainReward: the mean reward the optimiser saw on its own fresh prompts since the last checkpoint, against held-out correctness. firstHalf and secondHalf split the checkpoints after step 0 in two. n/a means one of the two series did not move (a constant series has no correlation).

speed.about: Milliseconds per REINFORCE step in Node (V8), one process, nothing else running: sample 3 answer words (3 forward passes) and one backward pass, at batch 8 (a lab size) and batch 32 (the fill's). msPerEval scores one checkpoint (256 prompts, sampled and greedy). inPool is the mean step time inside the fill's runs, 4 processes at once. A browser lab running 40 ms slices fits about 40 / ms steps per slice.

film.about: What the films draw. curves: for the step-200 start, each checker, each seed (1, 2, 3), the reward under that run's own checker and the correctness on the held-out prompts at every checkpoint (every 25 steps), and the share of answers that stop with ".". examples: seed 1's answers to the first 6 held-out prompts before and after training (800 steps), as words: greedy is the top word at every step, sampled is one draw with sampling seed 7; "." appears when the answer stopped.
